passage:
Scientists planted seeds from an old collection to see if they could still grow. Some did. The plants were carefully studied, not treated as curiosities.
Students learned that seeds can sleep for a long time under the right conditions.
The teacher connected the experiment to food security and biodiversity. Old seeds may contain traits useful for future farming.
The growing plants made the past alive in a literal way.
A seed is both memory and possibility. It carries instructions from an earlier world and waits for conditions to speak again through leaves.
